content:
olivia-cust: Hey, on Safari 16.4 users see streaming stop mid-response after ~20-40s. We get partial event data then EventSource 'error' event, reconnects but server never resumes. Works fine on Chrome.
support-ian: Sorry about that — can you share request/response headers and whether you're behind a CDN? Also which Safari exact version + mac/ios?
olivia-cust: Safari 16.4 on macOS 13.2 and iOS 16.4. We're behind CloudFront -> Cloudflare. Route is /v1/stream/chat SSE. I looked at a HAR and saw an initial 200 then later a 304 for the same resource, waterfall shows OPTIONS preflight then GET, then a 304 followed by stream cut.
maria-eng: 304 on SSE is suspicious. SSE must be served with no caching. Can you paste the response headers from the GET that started streaming?
olivia-cust: Headers from the GET that opened the stream:

HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/event-stream
cache-control: max-age=0, must-revalidate
connection: keep-alive
transfer-encoding: chunked
etag: "abc123"
vary: Accept-Encoding
access-control-allow-origin: https://app.customer.com
access-control-allow-credentials: true

Then after ~30s the client saw:

HTTP/2 304 Not Modified
cache-control: max-age=0, must-revalidate
etag: "abc123"

support-ian: That 304 likely came from an intermediary honoring If-None-Match. Safari's EventSource can react poorly when the edge sends 304 for a long-lived GET — it may close the stream. Also H2 multiplexing + edge optimizations sometimes coalesce frames and expose weird timing. We should prevent caching on SSE responses: set Cache-Control: no-store or no-cache, no-transform, and remove ETag/Vary where possible.
samir: Also check preflight OPTIONS caching. If OPTIONS is cached and later returned as 304, Safari might handle the subsequent GET differently. For CORS with credentials you need Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and exact origin, but set Access-Control-Max-Age small or 0 for SSE routes.
maria-eng: Quick repro I ran: Cloudflare returns 304 when ETag is present. Fix was to remove ETag for SSE endpoints or set Cache-Control: no-store. CloudFront/CF cache rules sometimes rewrite headers; ensure your CDN bypass rule for streaming paths.
support-ian: Workaround for clients: use a fetch+ReadableStream polyfill instead of native EventSource on affected Safari versions (TextDecoder/TextEncoder + newline splitting) — avoids some OS-level EventSource quirks.
olivia-cust: Could you give exact header set to recommend to our infra team?
maria-eng: Sure — sample server headers to disable caching & improve Safari compatibility:

Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform
Connection: keep-alive
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.customer.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Length

Also remove ETag and Vary for this path on the CDN. On CloudFront set TTL = 0 or create a behavior that bypasses cache for /v1/stream/* and whitelist Origin header if you need per-origin CORS.
support-ian: Notes on CDN edge config: avoid any 304-producing logic for streaming endpoints. If your origin returns ETag and the edge replies 304 the stream will be terminated. Bypass cache or use no-store.
maria-eng: Additional notes: Some proxies will also gzip/chunk differently (Vary: Accept-Encoding). no-transform helps; explicit no-store is more deterministic. If you must allow caching elsewhere, make the streaming route exempt.
samir: If you still see cutoffs after disabling cache, capture HAR + tcpdump on the server side. Look for RST/FIN frames or early stream termination from the proxy (FIN from edge). Also check HTTP/2 GOAWAY or SETTINGS frames that coincide with the cutoff.
olivia-cust: Thanks. We'll disable CDN cache for the stream path and remove ETag. One more Q: does H2 vs H1 matter here?
samir: H2 can make it more visible because of multiplexing; some intermediaries optimize H2 connections and may coalesce or respond with 304s differently. That said, the root cause here is caching and ETag interaction with long-lived GETs.
maria-eng: I'll create a short docs snippet for streaming endpoints and push to infra: header examples + CDN rules + recommended polyfill for clients.
support-ian: Filing an escalation to eng-frontend so we can update SDKs and docs. @eng-frontend-bot please assign.
eng-frontend-bot: Ticket INC-2026 created and assigned to maria-eng, samir. Priority: P2.
support-bot: Customer updated, suggested mitigation steps sent.
maria-eng: Target: update CDN behavior + remove ETag for streaming routes in 48h. If customer can patch earlier they should see immediate improvement.
olivia-cust: Implementing changes now, will report back after verification. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
